title: Embedded Collective Governance and Firm Strategy: The Case of New Zealand’s Māori Advisory Committee: Economic Research Working Paper No. 101
content: Firms increasingly build competitive advantage on cultural resources whose value derives from collective meaning, yet existing institutions either remove those symbols from the market or fail to protect them in time. We study the concept of embedded collective governance (ECG) for the use of traditional cultural expression: a governance form that embeds culturally-informed community review directly within market access institutions. We argue that ECG operates through two channels. Screening regulates entry at the registration gate. Certification rewards cultural alignment at the renewal margin, generating a premium for trademarks that survive culturally informed community review. We test ECG at the trademark level and the portfolio level using New Zealand’s 2003 Trademarks Act, which placed a Māori Advisory Committee (MAC) within the trademark system. Results confirm both channels: Māori related trademarks are less likely to be registered and expire in New Zealand relative to abroad.
